key_points: District House dorm has 16+ fire alarms in one semester
Thurston had crabs reported first week of school
Mount Vernon Campus shuttle is overcrowded, cuts frequency
GW is not a sports or school-spirit school by students' own admission
Weak sense of community; cliques reported among Black students
Political activism is prominent; protests, bomb threats disrupt campus life
Dining quality consistently described as declining and getting worse each year
Chartwells contract blamed for poor quality and limited chef creativity
Mislabeled food including allergens is a documented safety issue
CAPS counseling only offers appointments every two weeks due to demand
Students with serious depression left without adequate support options
TimelyCare and pay-what-you-can clinic exist as overflow alternatives
Financial aid office gives contradictory information depending on who answers
Processing delays leave students without funds weeks into semester
New free tuition under $100k income policy is significant but applies only to new students
Elliott School and international affairs programs are genuinely well-regarded
Non-politics programs like STEM are considered weak relative to peers
Blackboard LMS is outdated and widely disliked by students
Budget cuts are ongoing with staff reductions and course cancellations
Everything moves to Zoom even when staff are physically on campus
GW Alert system is vague and never explains incidents after the fact
Being in DC is the school's single biggest genuine selling point
Foggy Bottom location means Whole Foods is your closest grocery option
Sirens, homeless encampments, and DC street life are part of daily reality
DC location provides real internship access that competitors cannot match
Government internships described as frozen under Trump administration by current students
International students worry most DC jobs require US citizenship
Total cost approaching $98k per year for returning students
New free tuition policy for under $100k income is meaningful but limited
Students feel tuition increases while services like dining and counseling decline
DC is the draw; the university itself generates little loyalty or pride
Students who love GW love the city, not the institution
Political and international affairs students are most satisfied; others feel misled
**Finances**: Tuition raised $10k+ while financial aid was simultaneously cut for same students
**Safety**: Bomb threats, repeated gas leak fire alarms, and vague GW Alert with no follow-up
**Administration**: GW fudged US News data in 2012 and is still recovering ranking penalty
New free tuition for families under $100k is one of the best aid models in DC
